clean_body: | | | | | | | MONTGOMERY, Ala. (WBMA) — U.S. Senator Katie Britt applauded the unanimous decision by the U.S. House of Representatives Committee on Energy and Commerce to advance Lulu’s Law to the House floor. The bipartisan legislation, named after 16-year-old Lulu Gribbin who survived a near-fatal shark attack in June 2024, aims to allow shark attacks to be included in wireless emergency alerts. | | DOTHAN, Ala. (WTVY) - U.S. Senator Katie Britt (R-Alabama) announced Wednesday that through the recent passage of two 2026 fiscal year appropriations bills, she was able to secure over $2 million dollars in federal funding for the Wiregrass region. **1\. Trump Blinks on Greenland -- Again**
* David Shuster opens with Trump's latest bluff collapsing, this time over Greenland.
* Trump publicly admitted he _could_ use overwhelming force--but "won't," reinforcing a pattern of threats followed by retreat.
* Shuster notes the significance: restraint from a president who increasingly appears unstable is not reassuring--it's alarming.

**2\. A President Who Appears Unwell**
* Shuster highlights Trump's visible bruising and repeated confusion between Greenland and Iceland.
* That confusion had real-world consequences, triggering a stock market dip after Trump's erratic remarks.
* His speech at an economic summit is described as bizarre, rambling, and historically ignorant.
* * *

* * *

**3\. Ignorance on the World Stage**
* Trump falsely claimed European nations would be speaking German or Japanese without the U.S.
* Shuster points out the irony: German _is_ Switzerland's primary language.
* The segment underscores how Trump's bluster consistently collapses under basic facts.

**4\. A Stark Contrast: Real Leadership Emerges**
* Shuster contrasts Trump with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney.
* Carney's speech emphasized shared responsibility, realism, and collective action.
* The comparison frames Trump as chaotic while Canada projects steady, adult leadership.

* * *

**5\. Jack Smith 's Testimony and Trump's Meltdown**
* Former Special Counsel Jack Smith testified that evidence showed Trump committed crimes beyond a reasonable doubt.
* Trump responded with an unhinged social media spree.
* Shuster frames this as further proof of Trump's inability to function under accountability.

**6\. ICE Raids, Recklessness, and Karma**
* Shuster calls current ICE raids "arguably criminal," citing warrantless actions and lack of due process.
* He spotlights ICE leadership incompetence, including a chemical agent mishap that blew back on officers.
* Nature delivers poetic justice as brutal winter storms blanket much of the U.S.

Parents look to the government for guidance on what vaccines their children need and when to get them. These recommendations must be based on sound science — not conspiracy theories or political pressure.
**Every vaccine on the previous schedule has been extensively tested and safely administered to millions of children.**
Removing them without scientific justification undermines the medical community, sows distrust in our healthcare system, and will lead to thousands of preventable illnesses and deaths.
This rollback of decades-long public health progress is especially egregious as millions of Americans are losing access to lifesaving care due to the gutting of Medicaid and ACA subsidies by Trump and his Republican lapdogs in Congress.
_We cannot let RFK Jr. and political appointees override medical experts and endanger our children._
[As a physician, I took an oath to do no harm. RFK Jr.'s decision violates everything I believe in about medicine and public health. # [](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/43706?t=1&akid=240632%2E444211%2E9rNqqs)
My name is Darrel, and I’m proud to serve as a regional organizer with Powered by People, working on the ground across North DFW.
I want to share a bit of my journey and why this work matters so deeply to me.
I first stepped into politics by running for city council, a race I lost by just two votes. That two-vote margin made something very clear to me: organizing matters, and every conversation counts. Instead of walking away, I leaned in. In 2024, I ran for Texas House District 89. I didn’t win that race either, but what I gained was a deeper understanding of what it takes to build _real, lasting Democratic power._
For the past five years, I’ve stayed in the fight as a precinct chair and by taking on leadership roles within the Collin County Democratic Party. Those experiences prepared me for the work I’m now doing every single day.
Today, as Powered by People’s regional organizer for North DFW, I oversee a large and diverse 13-county area. That includes high-priority counties like Denton, Collin, and Hunt, as well as rural and underserved counties like Grayson, Lamar, Delta, Hopkins, Clay, and several others. Many of these communities have little to no Democratic infrastructure, and that is where our work is most urgent.
My job is to recruit and train local hosts, register new voters, support volunteers, and help build sustainable Democratic organizing in places that are too often overlooked.
**This is long-term, people-powered work, and I can tell you from personal experience that it only happens with grassroots support.**
**[That is why I’m asking today if you’ll chip in $3 to Powered by People’s work. Your contribution helps us train and support new local organizers and volunteers, expand voter registration efforts into rural and hard-to-reach counties, and build durable Democratic infrastructure across North Texas.](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/56109?c0=pbp-em-20260123.GNs-po&refcode=ema20260123-240632&t=3&akid=240632%2E444211%2E9rNqqs)**
**[Donate $3](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/56109?c0=pbp-em-20260123.GNs-po&refcode=ema20260123-240632&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=22&akid=240632%2E444211%2E9rNqqs)**
Every step forward, every new volunteer, every new voter, every new host, every new event is possible because people like you choose to invest in this work.
Thank you for believing in the power of grassroots organizing and for standing with us as we build a stronger, more inclusive future for North Texas.
In solidarity,
Darrel
Regional Organizer, North DFW, Powered by People

FROM: Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand, DSCC Chair
RE: Democrats’ Roadmap to a Senate Majority in 2026
As we approach the midterms, Senate Democrats are ready to compete everywhere, particularly in key battleground states.
Democrats have recruited the most formidable candidates possible across multiple battleground states, while Republicans have been bogged down by divisive primaries, recruitment failures, and a toxic agenda that voters are rejecting.
Not only do we have strong candidates and a favorable political environment, but we also have proven messaging. We are the party that will cut costs, stand up for democracy, and fight for working-class families. Republicans will jack up prices, let Trump do whatever he wants, and they only care about their billionaire donors.
With strong political tailwinds and even stronger candidates - here’s a breakdown of our top flip opportunities.
Top Flip Opportunities
1. North Carolina - We recruited Gov. Roy Cooper – a proven Democratic leader who’s never lost an election.
2.
3. Ohio - Sherrod Brown stepped up to run. He is beloved statewide with name recognition, and running against an appointed opponent. Maine - Susan Collins is in her weakest position ever as she faces down a tough Democrat challenge.
4.

6.

8.

Folks, the path is clear, but we only cross the finish line with an unprecedented level of grassroots support.

We can’t just win in one place – we have to win everywhere. We have to invest everywhere.

These six states present our best opportunities to flip seats and take back the Senate from MAGA extremists. Kirsten
